title: DSA5105 exam & homework map
summary: A revision index built from local exam evidence and public homework or midterm previews. Lecture scope remains the learning core; assessment evidence decides which moves deserve timed practice.
disclaimer: This is a study-priority map, not an official NUS assessment specification. Local exam PDFs are stronger evidence than third-party previews. A topic appearing here does not prove that every variation will be examined.

topics.title: Learning setup, risk, and validation/test
topics.lectureScope: Define the dataset, oracle, hypothesis space, empirical risk, population risk, and the train/validation/test boundary.
topics.examMove: Translate a word problem into the objects being observed, the objective being optimised, and the data split that may be used for a decision.
topics.practice: Explain why using test accuracy for model selection turns the test set into validation data.

topics.title: Linear basis, OLS uniqueness, and weighted risk
topics.lectureScope: Move from basis features to normal equations, rank conditions, and weighted empirical risk.
topics.examMove: State the rank assumption before using an inverse, then identify what changes when observations receive weights.
topics.practice: Derive the uniqueness condition and explain what rank deficiency does to the coefficient vector.

lectureRefs.role: past-exam dual ridge and validation alignment

topics.title: SVM duality, KKT conditions, and support vectors
topics.lectureScope: Connect the margin problem, dual variables, complementary slackness, and the points that remain active.
topics.examMove: Write the dual objective or KKT conditions, then use complementary slackness to classify support vectors.
topics.practice: Given a candidate alpha pattern, check balance, box constraints, margin activity, and whether the primal separator can be reconstructed.

topics.title: Decision trees, bagging, and AdaBoost
topics.lectureScope: Separate a local impurity reduction from the bias/variance reason that ensembles can help.
topics.examMove: Compute or compare a split, state the effect of depth, and explain how bagging or boosting changes the error pattern.
topics.practice: Derive the stump or split decision, then justify whether the ensemble primarily addresses variance, bias, or hard examples.

topics.title: Gradient descent, neural composition, and backpropagation
topics.lectureScope: Track a computation graph forward, then multiply local derivatives in reverse without confusing a gradient step with a global optimum.
topics.examMove: Name intermediate values, write local derivatives, and assemble the requested parameter gradient in the correct order.
topics.practice: Work one scalar graph by hand, then check signs, activation cases, and the parameter receiving each upstream signal.

topics.title: PCA, eigenvectors, reconstruction, and whitening
topics.lectureScope: Center first, form the covariance or Gram object, identify principal directions, and distinguish projection from whitening.
topics.examMove: Keep the centering convention visible, then connect eigenvalues to captured variance and reconstruction or whitening scale.
topics.practice: Complete a two-feature numerical PCA example without skipping centering or the eigenvector normalisation.

topics.title: K-means, GMM responsibilities, and EM
topics.lectureScope: Distinguish hard assignment from soft responsibility, and separate the E-step assignment from the M-step parameter update.
topics.examMove: Use old parameters for assignment, normalise responsibilities, and update only after the assignment is complete.
topics.practice: Calculate one responsibility or centroid update and state the objective being improved.

topics.title: MDPs, value iteration, TD(0), and replay
topics.lectureScope: Separate immediate reward, discounted continuation value, Bellman backup, TD error, and replayed experience.
topics.examMove: Write one backup from the transition information given, identify the target value, and state whether the update is on-policy or off-policy when relevant.
topics.practice: Perform two value-iteration sweeps and explain exactly where a future state's value enters.

topics.title: Graph kernels, PageRank, and power iteration
topics.lectureScope: Use Gram-matrix positive semidefiniteness and fixed-point iteration as two distinct graph reasoning patterns.
topics.examMove: Check the quadratic form or the stochastic transition convention before applying an eigenvalue or power-iteration argument.
topics.practice: Explain what is being preserved by the kernel representation and what damping changes in PageRank.

lectureRefs.role: past-exam graph kernel and PageRank alignment

topics.title: Graph Laplacians and spectral clustering
topics.lectureScope: Connect adjacency, degree, Laplacian energy, eigenvectors, and the final clustering step.
topics.examMove: State the matrix convention and interpret the selected eigenvectors before invoking K-means on the embedding.
topics.practice: Explain why a low-energy eigenvector gives a smooth graph partition and what the final K-means step still does.

topics.title: Ridge spectral filtering, LS-SVM KKT, and LOO
topics.lectureScope: Connect rank deficiency, positive regularisation, KKT block systems, leverage, and leave-one-out correction.
topics.examMove: State the invertibility assumption, identify the shifted spectrum or KKT block, and interpret the diagonal leverage term.
topics.practice: Explain why ridge can be unique when OLS is not, then use the same linear-algebra view to interpret LOO.

lectureRefs.role: past-exam dual ridge and validation alignment

topics.title: Dynamic programming and shortest-path recurrences
topics.lectureScope: Define the state, boundary, final-choice recurrence, evaluation order, and complexity before calculating.
topics.examMove: Derive the recurrence from the last move rather than guessing it from a memorised template.
topics.practice: Fill a small DP table and explain why each predecessor is sufficient.
